question: Do six non-blocking readiness/connection/usage families with no existing corpus guest (legacy accept, select, pselect6, ppoll, epoll_pwait each zero-timeout, and getrusage) hold byte-identical parity under e9patch preprocessing with the golden hermit ptrace backend?
backend: ptrace (golden reference); e9patch = binary-rewriting preprocessing, not a backend
determinism_level: L2 (--strict --verify, guest-visible bitwise-identical; detlog tail-match modulo 8-syscall e9loader prologue)
host_independence: prints only the syscall return on success (0) or a boolean valid-fd (1); zero-timeout readiness polls return immediately and register no timed waiter; getrusage fields read but never printed
gating: non-gated: zero-timeout readiness multiplexers block nothing and register no timed waiter; accept returns an already-pending connection; getrusage is read-only; routine backend-parity, no post-facto-human-review trigger
ci_note: e9tool/e9patch absent from CI (like KVM /dev/kvm); corpus harness ungated, only audit-inventory gates these files
note: First zero-drop round since r22. Confirmed hermit-SUPPORTED and now shipped: accept=43, select=23, pselect6=270, ppoll=271, epoll_pwait=281, getrusage=98. Field-thinning trend broke this round because the readiness-multiplexer family (select/pselect6/ppoll/epoll_pwait) is a rich vein of distinct, well-supported non-blocking syscalls analogous to the already-shipped poll_timeout_zero.
